_provenance.source: Anthony Bonner, The Art and Logic of Ramon Llull: A User's Guide
_provenance.locator: corpus lines 1866-1935; Llull ACIV (MOG I, vii, 9-10: 441-2)
_provenance.note: The moves below follow Bonner's report of Llull's worked example. Where the wording is compressed for play it is marked paraphrase; where Bonner quotes Llull it is marked quote.

attribution.why_labelled_this_way: Bonner mentions Bruno only twice, for the cosmological use of the combinatorics. Blum reports that Bruno's De compendiosa architectura recasts Lullian logic in Aristotelian terms; Mertens reports that what returns in Bruno is the similitudo-logic, not the letter notation. No evidence in this corpus that Bruno adopted Figure S. See docs/design/ENGINE.md section 1a.
attribution.brunos_version: Bruno's adaptation is a logica fantastica -- a logic whose operands are images held in the spiritus phantasticus, rather than Llull's letter-variables. That is why he must first build an image vocabulary (the atria and the image alphabet).

questions.title: Predestinatio et liberum arbitrium
questions.prompt: God's wisdom is perfect, and perfect wisdom foreknows all things. But if all is foreknown, what becomes of free will? Work the contradiction through the four figures.

stages.name: Figura prima
stages.name_en: The First Figure of X - affirmation
stages.situation: S enters the compartment of perfect wisdom in Figure A, in order to form the compartment of perfect predestination.
stages.quote: when E contemplates A, the compartment of perfect predestination is formed by necessary reasons, because if E remembered and understood predestination not to exist, it could not remember or understand perfect wisdom in A.

moves.label: Enter perfect wisdom, and affirm predestination
moves.result: Predestination follows necessarily from God's perfect wisdom. S is in E: remembering, understanding and loving what it affirms. But this causes a problem - N loves free will, which it now forgets and does not know.
moves.teaches: E is the state of informed acceptance. You remember, understand and love the thing affirmed.

moves.label: Refuse the compartment; deny predestination
moves.result: You cannot deny it from here without knowledge. Denying what you have not first understood drops S into N - supposition, credulity, belief without grounds.
moves.teaches: N is not a fault, but it is not knowledge. Llull calls it credulity: the will inclines without the memory or intellect having anything to work on.

stages.name: Figura secunda
stages.name_en: The Second Figure of X - denial
stages.situation: The contrary of the first in S. Substitute justice for wisdom in Figure A, and free will for predestination in Figure X.
stages.quote: The second figure of X is the contrary of the first in S, since as soon as E enters A by means of perfect justice, B remembers and C understands free will...

moves.label: Enter perfect justice, and affirm free will
moves.result: The mirror image. What began all for free will now turns against predestination for want of considering it. S is in I - still remembering and understanding, but now hating what it formerly affirmed.
moves.teaches: I is not failure. Informed rejection is as much a goal state as informed acceptance: to remember, understand and hate what is false is exactly the aim of the Art.

moves.label: Stay in perfect wisdom and hold predestination
moves.result: Nothing moves. Refusing to state the opposing case leaves you affirming one horn without ever having tested it, which the Art treats as an argument not yet made.
moves.teaches: The dialectic requires you to argue the contrary against yourself. An affirmation never subjected to its denial has not been demonstrated.

stages.name: Figura tertia
stages.name_en: The Third Figure of X - doubt
stages.situation: S finds itself confused in the First and Second Figures, with R joined to each of E I N. It therefore forms this third figure, the figure of doubt.
stages.quote: the wisdom of A strongly signifies predestination and the justice of A signifies free will equally strongly. But C G cannot at one and the same time understand perfect predestination or perfect free will, and thus C G are in doubt... and all of S is perverted into R.

moves.label: Hold both at once, and let S be perverted into R
moves.result: All positive and negative possibilities stand open at once. When R remembers, understands and loves free will, it forgets, misunderstands and hates predestination - and the reverse. You are stuck, and you are meant to be.
moves.teaches: R is confusion, and it is stage three of four, not a defeat. The Art requires the argument to jam before it can resolve. A dialectic that never reaches doubt has not tested anything.

moves.label: Pick the stronger horn and move on
moves.result: You have chosen rather than demonstrated. The Art does not adjudicate between the horns; a resolution reached by preferring one is the same argument you already made at stage one.
moves.teaches: Choosing a side is precisely what the fourth figure exists to avoid.

stages.name: Figura quarta
stages.name_en: The Fourth Figure of X - resolution
stages.situation: Place S, under the heading of E, in A, in the compartments of perfect power and perfect will, and the other compartments of A.
stages.quote: Now when C affirms these two compartments in A, it then affirms the compartment of predestination and free will.

moves.label: Re-enter A under perfect power and perfect will; affirm both horns
moves.result: The contradiction dissolves rather than being decided. Affirmed under power and will rather than under wisdom alone, predestination and free will are both compartments of the same perfect A. S returns to E - now holding what it could not hold at stage one.
moves.teaches: Resolution is not victory for one horn. It is finding the compartment at which both can be affirmed together. This is why the Art is a demonstration and not a debate.

moves.label: Re-enter under perfect wisdom alone
moves.result: Wisdom is the compartment that generated the problem. Entering by it again reproduces stage one, and S falls back into R.
moves.teaches: Escaping confusion means changing which dignity you enter by, not trying harder with the same one.
